rich_summary: This section recounts the downfall of Yavakri, illustrating the dangers of pride gained through boons and ascetic power. After obtaining supernatural knowledge of the Vedas, Yavakri’s father Bharadwaja warns him through the tale of Medhavi, a youth whose arrogance after receiving a divine boon led to his death when the condition sustaining his life was destroyed. Ignoring the warning, Yavakri grows reckless and insults other sages. When he lustfully approaches the daughter‑in‑law of the powerful sage Raivya, she cleverly reports the offense. Enraged, Raivya creates from his matted hair a woman and a demon through sacrificial rites and sends them to kill Yavakri. Deprived of ritual purity and divine protection, Yavakri is hunted, denied refuge, and slain by the demon’s spear. The episode underscores a central epic theme: spiritual power without humility leads inevitably to ruin.

highlight_spans.why: Yavakri boasts about his newly obtained boons and mastery of the Vedas, setting up the theme of pride that drives the tragedy.
The sages’ reflection that fate cannot be overcome summarizes the moral Bharadwaja tries to teach his son.
Yavakri’s shameless proposition to Raivya’s daughter‑in‑law marks the decisive moral transgression that triggers the revenge.
The climactic moment where the demon’s spear kills Yavakri, fulfilling the warnings about pride and misuse of ascetic power.

top_scenes.scene_text: The furious sage Raivya tears a matted lock of hair and casts it into the sacrificial fire, from which a demonic warrior and a woman emerge in the flames.
Yavakri runs in terror across a barren landscape as rivers and tanks appear mysteriously dried up while a spear‑wielding demon relentlessly pursues him.
At the doorway of Bharadwaja’s Agnihotra chamber, a blind Sudra guard restrains the desperate Yavakri as the demon hurls a spear that pierces his heart.
